msg: Ultra on root: The tm_dot_prod loop dominates (95.7% of cycles). Each 8-element iteration executes 16 byte loads (5 cycles each), 8 multiplies (5-6 cycles), 7 adds (3 cycles), and loop overhead. The requantization and fc overhead are negligible. Memory loads and multiply-add chains are the primary targets.

proposal.title: 4-element int8 dot product
proposal.semantics_c: uint32_t dot4(uint32_t rs1, uint32_t rs2) { int8_t a0=(int8_t)(rs1&0xFF), a1=(int8_t)((rs1>>8)&0xFF), a2=(int8_t)((rs1>>16)&0xFF), a3=(int8_t)((rs1>>24)&0xFF); int8_t b0=(int8_t)(rs2&0xFF), b1=(int8_t)((rs2>>8)&0xFF), b2=(int8_t)((rs2>>16)&0xFF), b3=(int8_t)((rs2>>24)&0xFF); return (uint32_t)((int32_t)a0*b0 + (int32_t)a1*b1 + (int32_t)a2*b2 + (int32_t)a3*b3); }
proposal.rationale: Replaces 4 lb (20 cycles), 4 mul (22 cycles), 3 add (9 cycles) = 51 cycles with 2 lw (10 cycles) + 1 dot4 (5 cycles) + 1 add (3 cycles) = 18 cycles per 4 elements. Two dot4 cover the 8-element loop body, yielding ~3.6x hotspot speedup. Uses 4 DSP multipliers + adder tree (~100 LUTs, 3.9% area).

proposal.title: 4-element dot product returning two 16-bit partial sums
proposal.semantics_c: uint32_t dot4p(uint32_t rs1, uint32_t rs2) { int8_t a0=(int8_t)(rs1&0xFF), a1=(int8_t)((rs1>>8)&0xFF), a2=(int8_t)((rs1>>16)&0xFF), a3=(int8_t)((rs1>>24)&0xFF); int8_t b0=(int8_t)(rs2&0xFF), b1=(int8_t)((rs2>>8)&0xFF), b2=(int8_t)((rs2>>16)&0xFF), b3=(int8_t)((rs2>>24)&0xFF); int16_t s0=(int16_t)((int32_t)a0*b0 + (int32_t)a1*b1); int16_t s1=(int16_t)((int32_t)a2*b2 + (int32_t)a3*b3); return (uint32_t)((uint16_t)s0 | ((uint32_t)(uint16_t)s1 << 16); }
proposal.rationale: Produces two independent 16-bit partial sums, enabling parallel reduction without 32-bit adder in critical path. Same load/mul savings as dot4 but final reduction uses two 16-bit adds (cheaper) then one 32-bit combine. Area similar to dot4 (~100 LUTs) but reduces register pressure.

proposal.title: 2-element int8 dot product
proposal.semantics_c: uint32_t dot2(uint32_t rs1, uint32_t rs2) { int8_t a0=(int8_t)(rs1&0xFF), a1=(int8_t)((rs1>>8)&0xFF); int8_t b0=(int8_t)(rs2&0xFF), b1=(int8_t)((rs2>>8)&0xFF); return (uint32_t)((int32_t)a0*b0 + (int32_t)a1*b1); }
proposal.rationale: Handles loop tail (size not multiple of 4) and can be used for 2-element chunks if dot4 not available. Replaces 2 lb (10 cycles), 2 mul (11 cycles), 1 add (3 cycles) = 24 cycles with 1 lw (5 cycles) + dot2 (5 cycles) = 10 cycles. Small area: 2 multipliers + 1 adder (~30 LUTs, 1.2%).

proposal.title: Requant multiply-add (sum*scale + bias)
proposal.semantics_c: uint32_t rqma(uint32_t rs1, uint32_t rs2) { int32_t sum = (int32_t)rs1; int16_t scale = (int16_t)(rs2 & 0xFFFF); int16_t bias = (int16_t)((rs2 >> 16) & 0xFFFF); return (uint32_t)((int32_t)sum * scale + bias); }
proposal.rationale: Fuses the multiply and add in requantization (sum = sum*scale + bias). The requant hotspot (0.94%) executes this once per output channel (64 times). Saves 1 mul (5 cycles) + 1 add (3 cycles) = 8 cycles per channel, ~500 cycles total. Area: 1 multiplier + 1 adder (~40 LUTs, 1.6%).

proposal.title: Requant arithmetic right shift
proposal.semantics_c: uint32_t rqsh(uint32_t rs1, uint32_t rs2) { int32_t val = (int32_t)rs1; uint32_t sh = rs2 & 0x1F; return (uint32_t)(val >> sh); }
proposal.rationale: Implements the variable arithmetic right shift (sum >> shift) in requantization. Saves shift instruction (3 cycles) per channel. Tiny cycle impact but very small area (barrel shifter reuse, ~10 LUTs, 0.4%). Can be combined with saturate.

proposal.title: Saturate int32 to int8
proposal.semantics_c: uint32_t sat8(uint32_t rs1, uint32_t rs2) { int32_t val = (int32_t)rs1; (void)rs2; if (val > 127) val = 127; else if (val < -128) val = -128; return (uint32_t)(int8_t)val; }
proposal.rationale: Final requant step: clamp to int8 range. Replaces 2-3 instructions (compare, branch, select). Saves ~5 cycles per channel. Area: two comparators + mux (~30 LUTs, 1.2%). Completes requant fusion with rqma and rqsh.

msg: Ultra on n2.1.1: The measured region spends 57% of executed instructions in ss_dot4_pair (4-element dot-product returning two 16-bit partials) and 33% in the tm_dot_prod loop overhead (loads, pointer updates, partial-sum accumulation, branch). Each 16-element chunk executes 4 custom instructions, 4 partial-sum unpack/add sequences, 8 loads, and pointer arithmetic. The requantization phase is only 3% of cycles. The dominant cycle consumers are the partial-sum reduction (shift+add+add per chunk) and the scalar accumulation into a 32-bit register.

Ultra on n1.1.1: The measured region is dominated by the tm_dot_prod loop (63% ss_dot4 intrinsics + 29% loop overhead) computing 64 independent 512-element int8 dot products. The requantization (3.6%) performs per-channel multiply-add-shift-saturate. The tail loop handles remainder elements with scalar mul-add. Cycle reduction must target the dot-product inner loop and requantization.

proposal.title: Dual-channel 2-element dot product
proposal.rationale: Enables 2-channel interleaving: rs1 holds 2 input elements per channel, rs2 holds 2 weight elements per channel. Replaces 2 ss_dot4 (2×6c) + 1 add (3c) + 2 extra loads (2×5c) = 28 cycles with 1 dot2x2 (6c) + 1 vadd16 (3c) + shared loads (2×5c) = 19 cycles per 4 elements per channel. Saves ~9 cycles per 4 elements × 512/4 × 64 channels ≈ 73k cycles (34% speedup on dot region). Uses 4 DSPs for four 8×8 multiplies.

proposal.title: Fused requantization (mul-add-shift-saturate)
proposal.rationale: Replaces the per-channel requant sequence (mul 5-6c + add 3c + variable shift ~3c + saturate branches ~5c = ~16 cycles) with one 6-cycle instruction. 64 channels × 10 cycles saved = 640 cycles (0.3% total). Packs scale, bias, shift into rs2 (16+16+4 bits). Uses one DSP for 32×16 multiply.

proposal.title: 8×8-bit signed multiply to 32-bit
proposal.rationale: Accelerates the tail loop (1-3 elements per channel) which currently does sign-extend (2 shifts, 6c) + 32×32 mul (5c) = 11 cycles per element. mul8 does sign-extend and multiply in one 6-cycle instruction using one DSP. 64 channels × 2 tail elements avg × 5 cycles saved = 640 cycles (0.3%).

proposal.title: Vector add of four 8-bit pairs
proposal.rationale: Provides 4 parallel 8-bit adds in 6 cycles vs 4×3=12 cycles for scalar adds. Could accelerate the 32-bit accumulation in tm_dot_prod by maintaining 8-bit partial sums with periodic carry propagation (software-managed), saving ~3 cycles per 4 dot4s. Also useful for vectorized bias add in requant if restructured. Estimated 0.1% total speedup. Purely combinational, no DSPs, minimal LUTs.

proposal.title: Fused 4-element int8 dot-product with 32-bit sum
proposal.rationale: Replaces dot4p (6 cycles) + srai (3) + add (3) + add (3) = 15 cycles/chunk with one 6-cycle instruction + one 3-cycle add = 9 cycles/chunk. Saves 6 cycles × 4 chunks × 2048 iters ≈ 49k cycles (21% of hotspot). Reuses the 4 DSP multipliers from existing dot4p; adds only a small 18-bit adder tree (~1% LUTs).

proposal.title: Horizontal add of two 16-bit halves
proposal.rationale: Generic reduction primitive: turns the two 16-bit partials from dot4p into a 32-bit sum in one 6-cycle instruction, replacing srai (3) + add (3) = 6 cycles. Saves 3 cycles/chunk (vs dot4p path) ≈ 24k cycles if dot4p retained; also useful for other SIMD reductions. Tiny area: one 16-bit adder (~0.5% LUTs).

proposal.title: SIMD add 4×int8 or 2×int16
proposal.rationale: Enables multi-channel accumulation: pack 2 channels' 16-bit partial sums (or 4 channels' 8-bit intermediates) into one register and add pairwise in 6 cycles vs 2× scalar adds (6 cycles) but with half the load/store pressure. Opens path to process 2 channels per loop iteration, cutting loop overhead (loads, pointer updates, branch) by ~30%. Area: four 8-bit adders (~1% LUTs).

proposal.title: Fused integer requantize (mul, add, shift, clamp)
proposal.rationale: Collapses the requant hotspot (3% cycles, but 64 calls × ~15 cycles = 960 cycles) into one 6-cycle instruction. Uses one DSP multiplier (free in LUT budget) + shifter + comparators (~2% LUTs). Completes the layer in the custom unit, removing all requant instructions from the pipeline.
